groups.title: The tour
groups.intro: Four short programs, each with breakpoints set where the specification's algorithms do the work. The debugger's guided script for them, stop by stop, is docs/debugger/DEMO.md.

groups.title: The language, step by step
groups.intro: Ordinary JavaScript, paused in the algorithms that give it its meaning: environments, calls into built-ins, eval, generators, modules.

groups.title: Corners of the specification
groups.intro: Programs that go where fewer readers go: Proxy traps, the job queue, using declarations, with, Annex B, regular expressions, top-level await, timeouts, iterator helpers.

groups.title: Errata: resolved readings and literal Assert stops
groups.intro: Each of these programs reaches a sentence documented on the Errata page (spec/DECISIONS.md). Where SpecTec bakes in the test262 or proposed reading, the program runs as engines and test262 expect; where SpecTec keeps the literal text, the run pauses and stops at the exact Assert or step where the text gives no answer.

groups.title: A proposal: import defer
groups.intro: Three programs that use the syntax of tc39/proposal-defer-import-eval. Under the specification's build each is a SyntaxError, since ECMA-262 has no such syntax. Under the build "Proposal: import defer", made from a branch where the proposal's text is merged into the specification's, each runs, and the breakpoints stop in the proposal's own algorithms.

groups.title: TC39 #117 agenda proposals (November 2026)
groups.intro: Thirteen more ECMA-262 proposals from the 117th TC39 plenary agenda (Stages 0–3, alongside import defer above). Each runs under its own lazy-loaded WebAssembly build and pauses inside the proposal's specification algorithm; under the baseline specification build each shows how ECMA-262 behaves today.

groups.title: The errata page's programs
groups.intro: Additional programs from the Errata page, opened under the specification build.

examples.title: A property get, up the prototype chain
examples.line: GetValue calls the object's [[Get]], which is OrdinaryGet; for a property the object lacks, OrdinaryGet calls its prototype's [[Get]] with the same receiver.
examples.name: get.js

examples.title: A function call
examples.line: EvaluateCall evaluates the arguments and calls Call, the function's [[Call]] makes a new execution context, and OrdinaryCallEvaluateBody runs the body.
examples.name: call.js

examples.title: A for-of loop
examples.line: ForIn/OfBodyEvaluation asks the iterator for its next result at step 8.a once per round, and once more to find that it is done.
examples.name: forof.js

examples.title: A throw caught
examples.line: The throw statement's Evaluation makes a throw completion inside the called function; it returns through [[Call]] to the try statement, and CatchClauseEvaluation binds it.
examples.name: throw.js

examples.title: IsCallable, step by step
examples.line: The worked example of How it works. EvaluateCall asks IsCallable of each callee that is an Object: a function has a [[Call]] internal method, and step 2 returns true; an ordinary object has none, step 3 returns false, and the call throws a TypeError.
examples.name: iscallable.js

examples.title: A let binding read before its declaration
examples.line: The declarative Environment Record's GetBindingValue finds the binding uninitialized and throws a ReferenceError, which the catch clause receives.
examples.name: s2_let_tdz.js

examples.title: A for loop's binding, copied each round
examples.line: ForBodyEvaluation calls CreatePerIterationEnvironment before the first round and after each, so each round has its own binding of i.
examples.name: loop.js

examples.title: An accessor property
examples.line: OrdinaryGet finds an accessor descriptor and, at step 7, calls its getter with the receiver as this; the getter's body runs in OrdinaryCallEvaluateBody.
examples.name: getter.js

examples.title: A built-in that calls back
examples.line: Array.prototype.map runs as a built-in function's steps under BuiltinCallOrConstruct, and calls the callback for each element; the JS stack shows the built-in between the two functions.
examples.name: map.js

examples.title: Direct eval and new Function
examples.line: A direct eval goes through PerformEval and new Function through CreateDynamicFunction; each parses its own source text, which the debugger opens as a source of its own.
examples.name: eval.js

examples.title: A generator
examples.line: Each yield is GeneratorYield, which suspends the generator's execution context; next() resumes it through GeneratorResume.
examples.name: generator.js

examples.title: A string that is not a directive
examples.line: "use strict" followed by .length on the next line is one expression statement, not a Use Strict Directive: IsStrict finds the script non-strict.
examples.name: strict.js

examples.title: Objects in the store
examples.line: Each debugger statement pauses; the Heap tab shows the object's cell, and after the assignment the cell that changed.
examples.name: heap.js

examples.title: Three modules
examples.line: The entry module's LoadRequestedModules, then Link, then Evaluate; each module of the bundle opens as a source of its own.
examples.name: bundle.js

examples.title: Proxy traps
examples.line: A get on a Proxy is the Proxy's own [[Get]], which calls the handler's get trap; every other trap is called the same way, and a missing one forwards to the target.
examples.name: proxy_traps.js

examples.title: Promise jobs in order
examples.line: then calls PerformPromiseThen, which makes a job with NewPromiseReactionJob; the jobs run after the script in the order they were queued, and resolving with a promise takes two more.
examples.name: promise_job_order.js

examples.title: using declarations
examples.line: At the end of the block, DisposeResources calls each resource's dispose method in the reverse order of the declarations; DisposableStack.prototype.dispose does the same.
examples.name: using_dispose.js

examples.title: The with statement
examples.line: Inside with, ResolveBinding goes through GetIdentifierReference to the object Environment Record's HasBinding, which reads @@unscopables.
examples.name: s2_with.js

examples.title: A function in a block, on a web browser's host
examples.line: With the host a web browser, FunctionDeclarationInstantiation also gives the enclosing function a var binding of the block's function (B.3.2.1): typeof f is undefined before the block and function after it.
examples.name: annexb_block_function.js

examples.title: Duplicate named groups
examples.line: Two groups of one name are an early error unless MightBothParticipate finds them in different alternatives; the check runs while the pattern is parsed.
examples.name: regexp_duplicate_named_groups.js

examples.title: Top-level await
examples.line: A module whose body awaits is evaluated by ExecuteAsyncModule, which runs the body with AsyncBlockStart, so the rest of the body runs from the promise jobs. Read literally, AsyncBlockStart's step 4 has no answer (erratum AsyncBlockStartAwaitResult) and the run stops there.
examples.name: module_top_level_await.js

examples.title: Timeouts after promise jobs
examples.line: The test host's setTimeout performs HostEnqueueTimeoutJob: the promise jobs run first, then each timeout job once its delay has passed on the host's clock.
examples.name: settimeout_order.js

examples.title: Iterator helpers
examples.line: Iterator.prototype.map and the other helpers make iterator objects whose next runs the helper's steps; Iterator.from, concat and zip build on the same protocol.
examples.name: iterator_helpers.js

examples.title: NumberMultiplyZeroSign: +0 × −5
examples.line: Number::multiply step 6 gives 𝔽(0), which is +0, where IEEE 754 and every engine give −0. The default reading gives −0, so 1 / (0 * -5) is -Infinity; the literal text gives +0 and Infinity.
examples.name: number_multiply_zero_sign.js

examples.title: SortInfiniteComparator: a comparator returning ±Infinity
examples.line: SortIndexedProperties takes ℝ of the comparator's result, which ±∞ does not have. The default reading orders by the result's sign; the literal text stops in SortIndexedProperties.
examples.name: errata_sort_infinite_comparator.js

examples.title: UnitChainChild: a labelled function in an if body
examples.line: IsLabelledFunction takes "the LabelledItem of" a Statement that has one only through its chain of single children. The default reading follows the chain and the early error makes it a SyntaxError; the literal text stops at IsLabelledFunction step 2.
examples.name: erratum_unit_chain_child.js

examples.title: AsyncBlockStartAwaitResult: an async function
examples.line: An async function's body runs under AsyncBlockStart and suspends at each await. Its step 4, read literally, has no answer for the result of the body's last await, and the run stops there; the default reading goes on, and the function's promise resolves to 2.
examples.name: async.js

examples.title: DoWaitSyncTimeout: Atomics.wait that times out
examples.line: On a host whose agent can block, DoWait waits until its timeout. The default reading gives the woken waiter the result "timed-out" and removes it from the WaiterList; as the text is written it returns "ok" and leaves the waiter in the WaiterList, so the second Atomics.wait fails AddWaiter step 2's Assert.
examples.name: atomics_wait_sync_timeout.js

examples.title: CreateDynamicFunctionPrivateIdentifiers: new Function with #names
examples.line: CreateDynamicFunction parses the parameters and the body on their own, where a private name refers to no class. The default reading makes that a SyntaxError for both (test262 requires it of the body); the literal text has no such check and makes the function.
examples.name: dynamic_function_private_identifiers.js

examples.title: UnregisterIteratesCopy: two cells with one token
examples.line: FinalizationRegistry.prototype.unregister removes cells from the list it iterates. The default reading removes both cells with the token, so a second unregister returns false; as written it skips the second cell, and the second call returns true.
examples.name: errata_unregister_two_cells.js

examples.title: GetUTCEpochNanosecondsNaN: a local time out of range
examples.line: setHours(1e21) asks UTC for a local time far out of range: GetUTCEpochNanoseconds finds no time value, and the Assert of its step 4 fails. SpecTec keeps the literal text here, so the run stops at the failed Assert.
examples.name: date_utc_large_local_time.js

examples.title: GetMatchStringStartAfterEnd: lastIndex inside a surrogate pair
examples.line: With /u and lastIndex on the second half of a surrogate pair, RegExpBuiltinExec starts the empty match at the pair's start, and GetMatchString's Assert (start before end) fails at step 1. SpecTec keeps the literal text here, so the run stops at the failed Assert.
examples.name: regexp_lastindex_inside_pair.js

examples.title: PromiseJobAbruptCompletion: a reaction job that throws
examples.line: A promise reaction job, made by NewPromiseReactionJob, returns a throw completion when the species constructor's resolve function throws, which a job must not do. SpecTec keeps the literal text here, so the run stops when the job returns.
examples.name: promise_job_abrupt.js

examples.title: import defer: a namespace evaluated at its first read
examples.line: With proposal-defer-import-eval, `import defer * as heavy` links heavy.mjs with the graph but leaves it unevaluated: InitializeEnvironment asks GetModuleNamespace for its ~defer~ namespace, and the first read of an export goes through the namespace's [[Get]] and GetModuleExportsList to EvaluateModuleSync. Reading %Symbol.toStringTag% does not evaluate it.

printed: main starts; heavy evaluates; read 42; read again 42

examples.name: import_defer_basic.js

examples.title: import.defer(): a promise for an unevaluated namespace
examples.line: `import.defer()` loads and links the module, and ContinueDynamicImport's ~defer~ branch asks GatherAsynchronousTransitiveDependencies what must be evaluated first (nothing here) before it settles the promise. The module exports `then`, but a deferred namespace has no `then` (IsSymbolLikeNamespaceKey), so settling the promise does not evaluate it; reading `x` does.

printed: promise settled; then in ns: false; dep evaluates; x is 1

examples.name: import_defer_dynamic.js

examples.title: import defer and top-level await
examples.line: The proposal's README graph: c is deferred, but its dependency d awaits at top level, so InnerModuleEvaluation asks GatherAsynchronousTransitiveDependencies for c's asynchronous dependencies and evaluates d (and e) with the graph; f and c wait for the first read of c's namespace, which EvaluateModuleSync evaluates synchronously.

printed: before access: b, e, d, a
after access: b, e, d, a, f, c

examples.name: import_defer_tla.js

examples.title: Stage 3: Import Text (with { type: "text" })
examples.line: HostLoadImportedModule dispatches on the type: "text" import attribute to CreateTextModule, wrapping the UTF-8 decoded text in a Synthetic Module Record shared between static and dynamic imports.

printed: Hello from ECMA-262 Import Text! | cached=true

examples.name: proposal_import_text.js

examples.title: Stage 3: Thenable Curtailment
examples.line: Promise.resolve inspects whether looking up "then" could run user code via RequiresDeferredPromiseResolution, then dispatches user-defined thenables through PerformPromiseResolveThenable.
examples.name: proposal_thenable_curtailment.js

examples.title: Stage 2.7: Deferred Re-exports (export defer)
examples.line: Importing barrel.mjs links export defer { x } from "./heavy.mjs" without evaluating heavy.mjs; reading barrel.x triggers EnsureDeferredExportEvaluated on the module namespace.
examples.name: proposal_deferred_reexports.js

examples.title: Stage 2.7: JSON.parse Options (freeze & nullPrototypeObjects)
examples.line: CreateJSONParseOptions validates the options bag for { freeze: true } and { nullPrototypeObjects: true }, producing frozen null-prototype graphs or mutable null-prototype objects.
examples.name: proposal_json_parseimmutable.js

examples.title: Stage 2.7: ESM Phase Imports (import source & ModuleSource)
examples.line: import source and import.source() bind a ModuleSource object inheriting from %AbstractModuleSource%; dynamic import(depSrc) unwraps its Module Source Record via GetModuleSourceRecord and coalesces evaluation.
examples.name: proposal_esm_phase_imports.js

examples.title: Stage 2.7: Immutable ArrayBuffers
examples.line: sliceToImmutable copies a subrange and transferToImmutable detaches the source buffer into a new buffer with [[ArrayBufferDetachKey]] ~immutable~, causing TypedArray writes to throw a TypeError.
examples.name: proposal_immutable_arraybuffer.js

examples.title: Stage 2: Error.code property
examples.line: Error, NativeError, and SuppressedError constructors delegate to InstallErrorOwnProperties, installing non-enumerable code alongside cause from the options object.
examples.name: proposal_error_code_property.js

examples.title: Stage 2: Math.fusedMultiplyAdd
examples.line: For a = 1 + 2^-52 and b = 1 - 2^-52, naive a * b + (-1) rounds a * b to 1 first and yields 0; Math.fusedMultiplyAdd computes a * b + c in R with a single rounding, preserving -2^-104.
examples.name: proposal_fma.js

examples.title: Stage 2: Composites
examples.line: Composite(...) canonicalizes integer-index keys before lexicographic string keys, freezes the object with null prototype, and interns structural duplicates in the Realm's [[CompositeRegistry]].
examples.name: proposal_composites.js

examples.title: Stage 1: Cancellation (AbortController & AbortSignal)
examples.line: new AbortController() allocates an AbortSignal via CreateAbortSignal; a block-scoped using registration disposes cleanly before ac.abort("timeout") runs SignalAbort and rejects Atomics.waitAsync.
examples.name: proposal_cancellation.js

examples.title: Stage 0: Iterator.prototype.transfer
examples.line: Iterator.prototype.transfer moves a suspended generator's state and execution context onto a fresh Generator instance while marking the source generator ~completed~.
examples.name: proposal_iterator_transfer.js

examples.title: Stage 0: Trim Specific Characters
examples.line: String.prototype.trim accepts an optional characters string and forwards it to TrimString, which trims matching Unicode code points via StringToCodePoints rather than UTF-16 code units.
examples.name: proposal_trim_chars.js

examples.title: Stage 0: Bitwise counting (Math.popcount32 & Math.ctz32)
examples.line: Math.popcount32 counts 1 bits and Math.ctz32 counts trailing 0 bits of ToUint32(n), returning 32 when the 32-bit unsigned value is 0.
examples.name: proposal_popcount.js

examples.title: StringValueReservedWord: an escaped reserved word
examples.line: var \u0069f spells the reserved word if with an escape; the default reading makes it a SyntaxError.
examples.name: erratum_stringvalue_reserved_word.js

examples.title: LookaheadSourceTokens: let and a newline
examples.line: After if (0) let and a line break, ExpressionStatement's lookahead reads the source's tokens past the inserted semicolon; the default reading gives no parse, a SyntaxError.
examples.name: erratum_lookahead_source_tokens.js

examples.title: HTMLCloseCommentToken: --> on the first line
examples.line: On a host with B.1.1, a first-line --> is an HTMLCloseComment; the default reading takes it as a comment, and the program gives 1.
examples.name: erratum_html_close_comment_token.js

examples.title: AnnexBRegExpOrder: /\b*/
examples.line: Under B.1.2's grammar the alternatives commit in order: \b is an Assertion, which no quantifier follows, so the pattern is a SyntaxError.
examples.name: erratum_annexb_regexp_order.js

examples.title: AnnexBGroupCount: /(a)\1/
examples.line: Under B.1.2's grammar \1 with one capturing group is a backreference: the group count comes from a committed parse.
examples.name: erratum_annexb_group_count.js

examples.title: AnnexBModifierEarlyErrors: /(?ii:a)/
examples.line: §22.2.1.1's modifier rules apply to B.1.2's ExtendedAtom under the default reading: a repeated modifier is a SyntaxError.
examples.name: erratum_annexb_modifier_early_errors.js

examples.title: CoveredNodeParent: a tail call in parentheses
examples.line: The covered ParenthesizedExpression takes its cover's place in the tree, so return (f(n - 1)) is in tail position.
examples.name: erratum_covered_node_parent.js

examples.title: BuiltinReturnCompletion: Array.fromAsync's result
examples.line: Array.fromAsync's promise is fulfilled with the array under the default reading of BuiltinCallOrConstruct step 10.b.iii.
examples.name: builtin_async_return.js

examples.title: ExecuteModuleAsyncDisposeResources: await using in a module
examples.line: A module with top-level await disposes its await using resources after its body under the default reading; read literally, never.
examples.name: errata_execute_module_dispose.js

examples.title: IdentityEscapeJoinControls: \ before ZWNJ and ZWJ
examples.line: Without the u or v flag, a backslash before U+200C or U+200D is an IdentityEscape under the default reading.

printed: U+200C: literal true, class true, a-literal true, RegExp true, u SyntaxError, v SyntaxError
U+200D: literal true, class true, a-literal true, RegExp true, u SyntaxError, v SyntaxError
U+200B: literal true, class true, a-literal true, RegExp true, u SyntaxError, v SyntaxError
U+200E: literal true, class true, a-literal true, RegExp true, u SyntaxError, v SyntaxError
U+61: literal SyntaxError, class SyntaxError, a-literal SyntaxError, RegExp SyntaxError, u SyntaxError, v SyntaxError
U+B7: literal SyntaxError, class SyntaxError, a-literal SyntaxError, RegExp SyntaxError, u SyntaxError, v SyntaxError

examples.name: regexp_identity_escape_join_controls.js

examples.title: AllocateSharedArrayBufferByteLengthStore: a growable SharedArrayBuffer
examples.line: grow reads the byte length that AllocateSharedArrayBuffer stored in a Shared Data Block.
examples.name: errata_allocate_sab_byte_length.js

examples.title: ContainsAwaitCover: await in parameters
examples.line: The early errors "X Contains AwaitExpression" see an await expression, which parses as a cover.

printed: async arrow in async body: SyntaxError
await in async body: no error
static block in async function: no error
var await in nested function: no error
var await in static block function: no error

examples.name: await_in_params_early_errors.js

examples.title: SplitCodeUnitStrings: "ab".split("")
examples.line: Each element is a String of one code unit under the default reading; read literally, the Array holds code units.
examples.name: errata_split_code_units.js

examples.title: CreateIntrinsicsAsyncArgument: an accessor's name and Array.fromAsync
examples.line: Under the default reading a getter gets its prefix and Array.fromAsync is async.
examples.name: errata_createintrinsics_async_argument.js

examples.title: IsCharacterClassControlLetter: /[\c1-\c5]/
examples.line: On a host with B.1.2, a class range between two \c escapes asks IsCharacterClass of each; the default reading gives that production a row.
examples.name: errata_ischaracterclass_control_letter.js

examples.title: BigIntMaximumSize: 1n << 2n ** 31n
examples.line: The proposed text throws a RangeError past the implementation's maximum BigInt size; read as written, the engine stops at its own limit.
examples.name: bigint_huge_left_shift.js
